top_stories.title: 4.5-billion-year-old Sahara meteorite may be the first clue to a lost planet that vanished from our solar system | - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: A meteorite, **NWA 12774**, found in the Sahara Desert has sparked debate among scientists about early solar system formation. The angrite meteorite, a rare type of volcanic rock, contains unusual mineral patterns and high-pressure clinopyroxene crystals that suggest it formed under conditions far more intense than expected for small asteroids. This discovery challenges previous assumptions about how planets developed and suggests the parent body of NWA 12774 may have been significantly larger than previously thought, potentially reaching a size comparable to a moon.  The findings raise questions about the completeness of our understanding of early planetary formation and highlight the need for further research on overlooked fragments in meteorite collections.

top_stories.title: Who is Mahender Makhijani? Indian-origin businessman accused of hosting sex parties and blackmailing attendees in $100 million fraud case - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Mahender Makhijani**, an Indian-origin financier, was arrested on Wednesday in California after a federal raid on his mansion. He is accused of running a $100 million bank fraud scheme involving falsified real estate documents and inflated property values. **Makhijani** used **Cantor Group V LLC** and a network of companies to carry out the scheme, which defrauded a local bank.  He also allegedly hosted parties with sex workers, using this information to blackmail attendees and exert control over employees and associates. He faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted. The case overlaps with a long-running business dispute involving **Hotel Laguna**, where Makhijani is accused of breaching agreements and committing fraud.

top_stories.title: Hero’s welcome for Somali referee denied entry to US World Cup tournament | Racism News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Omar Artan**, a Somali referee selected for the FIFA World Cup, was denied entry to the United States at Miami International Airport. **Donald Trump**'s administration cited unspecified "vetting concerns" as the reason for his refusal despite Artan having a valid visa and being exempt from travel bans under US State Department rules.  The decision has been met with widespread criticism, including from former presidents, prominent figures in international sport, and human rights advocates. **FIFA** stated that the matter fell under the jurisdiction of US immigration authorities, while **Somalia's Ministry of Youth and Sports** expressed disappointment over the situation and engaged in diplomatic efforts to resolve it.

top_stories.title: Kashmiri rights activist wins partial court victory but remains behind bars | Civil Rights News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Khurram Parvez**, a Kashmiri human rights activist, was granted partial bail in a "terror funding" case after nearly five years of imprisonment in India.  The Delhi High Court's decision came after he was arrested by the **National Investigation Agency (NIA)** for accusations of recruiting rebels and mobilizing protesters. Despite this victory, Parvez remains incarcerated in a separate case related to alleged "terror funding." International rights groups have condemned his arrest and continued imprisonment, highlighting concerns about political prisoners facing lengthy pre-trial detention under India's counterterrorism law.

top_stories.title: Pakistan military helicopter crashes in Kashmir, all on board killed | Military News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: A **Pakistan military** helicopter carrying personnel crashed near Muzaffarabad, killing all on board. The crash was attributed to a technical fault during takeoff and is under investigation by a board of inquiry.  The incident occurred amidst heightened security measures in the region following protests and clashes between protesters and authorities.

top_stories.title: Indian-origin billionaire offers Rs 2 crore package after 7 killed in Dubai crash | World News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: A deadly minibus crash in the UAE, which claimed seven lives and injured nine others, has prompted **Dr Shamsheer Vayalil**, chairman of **Burjeel Holdings**, a private healthcare group, to announce an over Rs 2 crore humanitarian assistance package. The crash involved a minibus carrying employees of a Dubai-based company that collided with a truck that had reportedly stopped due to a technical malfunction.  **Vayalil**'s support package includes compensation for the families of the deceased, treatment and recovery expenses for injured survivors, and emergency travel and accommodation costs for relatives.

top_stories.title: On Camera, Delhi Traffic Cop Hospitalised After SUV Tries To Run Him Over
top_stories.rephrased_article: A speeding black SUV attempted to run over traffic police in Delhi's New Friends Colony.  **Head Constable Rahul** was hit by the vehicle near the Sarai Julena red light and sustained injuries. The SUV fled the scene after hitting the officer, who is now hospitalized for treatment. **The police** have registered a case and are investigating the incident.

top_stories.title: West Bank ethnic cleansing, settler attacks Israel’s state policy: Amnesty | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Amnesty International** claims the displacement of Palestinians from the occupied West Bank is part of a deliberate Israeli government strategy of ethnic cleansing, not isolated settler violence. The report states that at least 117 villages have been affected by attacks and threats from settlers, forcing over 5,900 people to leave their homes between January 2023 and December 2025.  **Israel’s Security Cabinet** approved the establishment of 34 illegal settlements in the West Bank in April, further accelerating annexation efforts. **Amnesty International** urges the international community to prevent the destruction of Palestinian communities and the annexation of the West Bank.

top_stories.title: German Model Missing For Nearly 11 Years Named In Epstein Files: Report
top_stories.rephrased_article: **German** model "Michele" has been named in **Epstein** files, sparking fears for her disappearance.  The 22-year-old vanished from her home in September 2015 and had contact with a model recruiter, **Daniel Siad**, who is under investigation in France for aiding **Epstein**.  **Siad** allegedly sent **Epstein** photos of women, including "Michele," and claimed he would love her. The model's mother believes she may be deceased.
